description: FLARE-On 4 challenge set released in 2017 by FireEye FLARE team. The zip archive (8,293,788 bytes, SHA-256: 760f1130aa0166a25a50c334d5ecc1537a71e3761360fa17b83ab63a402748b7) contains 12 challenges across folders 01–12. Notable artifacts: challenge 01 (login.html, 877 bytes) is a client-side JavaScript authentication challenge where the flag 'ClientSideLoginsAreEasy@flare-on.com' is obscured via ROT13; challenge 02 (IgniteMe.exe, 3,072 bytes) is a tiny PE32 console binary with XOR-based key derivation (prompt: 'G1v3 m3 t3h fl4g:'); challenge 04 (notepad.exe, 76,288 bytes) is a trojanized Windows Notepad binary; challenge 08 (flair.apk, 3,848,256 bytes) is an Android APK; challenge 09 (remorse.ino.hex, 12,503 bytes) is an Arduino firmware hex file; challenge 10 (shell.php, 3,586 bytes) is an obfuscated PHP webshell with base64-encoded XOR payload and MD5-based key derivation; challenge 12 includes a filtered PCAP (20170801_1300_filtered.pcap, 5,747,603 bytes) alongside a PE binary (coolprogram.exe). The collection spans Windows PE, .NET, ELF Linux, Android APK, Arduino firmware, PHP webshell, and PCAP — one of the most technically diverse FLARE-On editions.

peirce_chain.firstness: 13 files in 12 challenge folders. File types: PE32 console (x4), PE32 GUI ELF 64-bit Linux (x1), PE32 DLL x86-64 (x1), Android APK (x1), Arduino Intel HEX (x1), PHP script (x1), HTML/JS (x1), pcap (x1), PE32 GUI x86 (x1). Size range: 877 bytes (login.html) to 5,747,603 bytes (PCAP). Archive is AES-256 encrypted with password 'flare'.
peirce_chain.secondness: No benign archive of this cross-platform composition exists. login.html demonstrates deliberate ROT13 obfuscation of an email flag — a technique used in real phishing infrastructure. shell.php is a functional obfuscated webshell (base64+XOR+MD5 key derivation) of a class actually deployed in the wild. remorse.ino.hex targets an embedded firmware platform rarely seen in CTFs, indicating intent to cover firmware RE. notepad.exe is a trojanized legitimate Windows binary — a masquerading technique (MITRE T1036.005) used in real APT toolchains.
peirce_chain.thirdness: The FLARE-On 4 collection deliberately cross-trains on the full threat surface: web (PHP shell, HTML/JS), mobile (APK), embedded (Arduino), network (PCAP), and Windows malware (PE32, DLL, .NET). Each challenge teaches a distinct class of adversarial technique encountered in real IR engagements. The PHP webshell (challenge 10) in particular is indistinguishable from real deployed webshells without dynamic analysis — a deliberate choice to force dynamic execution awareness. Carnegie pattern: authority — FLARE brand primes analysts to engage actively with content they would otherwise sandbox or destroy.

devil_advocate: A CTF competition archive is not malicious by design. All samples are provided for educational reverse engineering in a sandboxed context. The PHP webshell (shell.php) requires a password not provided in the archive — it cannot execute autonomously. The ROT13 flag in login.html is a pedagogical demonstration of why client-side authentication is insecure, not an active attack. The INTENT verdict applies to the technical intentionality of the challenges, not criminal deployment.

artifacts.description: Outer zip archive Flare-On4_Challenges.zip. SHA-256 verified against task specification. Size: 8,293,788 bytes. AES-256 encrypted (PK compat v5.1), password: 'flare'. Contains 13 files in 12 folders (challenges 01–12). Archive entry dates range 2017-04-28 to 2017-09-01.

Challenge 01 — login.html (877 bytes). HTML/JavaScript client-side authentication. The JavaScript applies ROT13 to user input and compares against hardcoded ciphertext 'PyvragFvqrYbtvafNerRnfl@syner-ba.pbz'. ROT13 decodes to 'ClientSideLoginsAreEasy@flare-on.com'. Technique: client-side auth / ROT13 obfuscation — illustrates that client-side secrets are trivially reversible. Flag confirmed: ClientSideLoginsAreEasy@flare-on.com.

metadata.file_type: HTML document, ASCII text, with CRLF line terminators

artifacts.description: Challenge 02 — IgniteMe.exe (3,072 bytes). PE32 console Intel 80386, 3 sections. Extremely compact PE (3 KB). Imports: GetStdHandle, ReadFile, WriteFile, ExitProcess (KERNEL32.dll only). Prompts 'G1v3 m3 t3h fl4g:' — leet-speak for 'give me the flag'. Responses: 'G00d j0b!' or 'N0t t00 h0t R we? 7ry 4ga1nz plzzz!'. Contains obfuscated key material: strings '&IE*', 'xD+l]^E', '+DonV_EGs&'. Technique class: XOR key derivation / minimal PE crackme.

artifacts.description: Challenge 04 — notepad.exe (76,288 bytes). PE32 GUI Intel 80386, 3 sections. Timestamp 2008-04-14 — predating the challenge by 9 years, suggesting this is a modified copy of the Windows XP/Vista Notepad binary. Trojanized system binary challenge — participants must identify modifications to a legitimate Windows binary. Technique class: binary diffing / trojanized system binary (T1036.005). MITRE T1036.005.

artifacts.description: Challenge 08 — flair.apk (3,848,256 bytes). Android package (APK) with AndroidManifest.xml and APK Signing Block. Name 'flair' may reference TGI Friday's 'flair' — a cultural in-joke. Largest non-PCAP artifact at 3.8 MB. Requires Android APK decompilation (jadx/apktool). Technique class: Android APK reverse engineering / Java/Dalvik RE.

artifacts.description: Challenge 09 — remorse.ino.hex (12,503 bytes). Arduino Intel HEX firmware file (ASCII text, CRLF). '.ino' extension indicates Arduino sketch source; '.hex' indicates compiled Intel HEX firmware. Requires AVR disassembly (avr-objdump or Ghidra AVR processor module). Unique in FLARE-On history as an embedded firmware challenge. Technique class: embedded firmware RE / AVR ISA disassembly.

metadata.file_type: ASCII text, with CRLF line terminators (Intel HEX format)
metadata.technique_class: Arduino firmware RE / AVR ISA / embedded systems

artifacts.description: Challenge 10 — shell.php (3,586 bytes). PHP webshell. Base64-encoded 2,268-byte payload XOR-decrypted with MD5-derived key from POST parameter 'o_o'. MD5 check: if MD5(decrypted) == '43a141570e0c926e0e3673216a4dd73d' → execute via create_function(). Structurally identical to real-world PHP webshells deployed in web server intrusions. Technique class: PHP webshell / base64+XOR obfuscation / password-protected backdoor (T1505.001, T1059.006). MITRE T1505.001.

metadata.file_type: PHP script, ASCII text, with very long lines (3586), with no line terminators

artifacts.description: Challenge 12a — 20170801_1300_filtered.pcap (5,747,603 bytes). libpcap v2.4 Ethernet capture. Filename encodes date 2017-08-01 13:00 'filtered' — suggests traffic was pre-filtered to contain only relevant streams. Paired with coolprogram.exe. Technique class: PCAP forensics / C2 channel identification / paired binary-traffic analysis (T1071).

metadata.file_type: pcap capture file, microsecond ts (little-endian) - version 2.4 (Ethernet, capture length 262144)

artifacts.description: Challenge 12b — coolprogram.exe (86,528 bytes). PE32 GUI Intel 80386, 9 sections. Name 'coolprogram' is deliberately banal — a masquerading tactic. 9 PE sections is unusually high and suggests runtime packing/unpacking or overlay data. Paired with 20170801_1300_filtered.pcap — this binary is the C2 client that generated or communicates with the PCAP traffic. Technique class: C2 client RE / paired binary+traffic analysis (T1071, T1027).

metadata.file_type: PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386, for MS Windows, 9 sections
metadata.technique_class: C2 client RE / packed PE / paired binary+traffic analysis (T1071, T1027)

known_limitations: shell.php payload (2,268 bytes XOR-decrypted content) was not fully decrypted — the password to derive the XOR key was not brute-forced or found. Payload type is INFERRED from structural analysis.
PCAP 20170801_1300_filtered.pcap was not parsed with tshark. Protocol breakdown, packet count, and C2 protocol identification are INFERRED from filename and size only.
No sandbox execution performed on any binary. Technique-class assignments for challenges 05, 07, 09, 11 are INFERRED from file metadata only.
Arduino remorse.ino.hex was not disassembled — AVR firmware analysis not performed.
Challenge 01 flag confirmed via static ROT13 reversal: ClientSideLoginsAreEasy@flare-on.com.
